title: Public site forms (contact and calls to action) submit into newsroom Messages
description:
As a publication without its own CRM, I can put simple forms on the public site (a contact form, a consultation or sponsorship request, any call-to-action button that opens a short form) and every submission lands in the newsroom's Messages, where editors triage, assign, mark handled and reply by email. Sites that do have a CRM can keep pointing their calls to action there; this is the built-in default.

Forms are defined as data (site config or backend data): an id, title, fields (name, email, topic choices, message, hidden context such as the page URL), the notification route, and the confirmation text. The site renders them; the backend receives them.

Public endpoint (shared with this milestone's newsletter signup work): unauthenticated, rate-limited, bot challenge (e.g. Turnstile) plus a honeypot, strict size limits, no input reflection. Each submission becomes a Message (messageKind form_submission, form id, fields, page URL, received-at) visible to editors and admins only, never through the guest or content API; email addresses are personal data handled like subscriber records. Optional notification (email or Slack) per form. The same messages are readable and answerable through the CLI so agents can triage them too.

Site contract: while a form's endpoint is not configured, the page says it is not open yet and never fakes a successful send. Pilot: Distinctive Mark, whose /contact/ page and Report-an-error links already post to contact.endpoint (null until this ships). Acceptance: a message sent from the live form appears in Messages within seconds; scripted posts are blocked; editors and agents can mark handled and reply.
